boards.title: 10 Late-Night Runs That Explain University of Missouri-Kansas City
boards.description: Ten under-21-safe Kansas City food stops with currently published late-hours information; confirm availability before leaving campus.

cards.title: Insomnia Cookies — Westport
cards.subtitle: 505 Westport Road, Kansas City, MO
cards.notes: Use the Westport listing to plan a cookie pickup; its posted Thursday–Saturday hours run as late as 3 a.m.
cards.short_summary: A cookie shop with clearly posted late-week hours.
cards.evidence_claim: The Westport listing posts hours until 3 a.m. Thursday through Saturday for Insomnia Cookies at 505 Westport Road.
cards.access_notes: Posted hours: 11 a.m.–3 a.m. Thursday–Friday and noon–3 a.m. Saturday; other days close at 1 a.m.

cards.title: Insomnia Cookies — Power & Light
cards.subtitle: 54 E. 14th Street, Kansas City, MO
cards.notes: Check the district’s venue page before heading downtown; it lists cookies, brownies, ice cream, and late daily hours.
cards.short_summary: Downtown cookies and desserts with a 3 a.m. posted close.
cards.evidence_claim: Power & Light District lists Insomnia Cookies at 54 E. 14th Street, open until 3 a.m. daily.
cards.access_notes: Posted hours: 9 a.m.–3 a.m. Monday–Friday and 11 a.m.–3 a.m. Saturday–Sunday.

cards.title: El Pueblito
cards.subtitle: 810 Southwest Boulevard, Kansas City, MO
cards.notes: For a weekend option, use the restaurant’s own hours page and aim for Friday or Saturday, when it lists a 4:30 a.m. close.
cards.short_summary: A Southwest Boulevard restaurant with very late weekend hours.
cards.evidence_claim: El Pueblito lists Friday and Saturday opening hours of 10 a.m.–4:30 a.m. at 810 Southwest Boulevard.
cards.access_notes: Posted Friday–Saturday hours end at 4:30 a.m.; Sunday–Thursday hours are listed through midnight.

cards.title: Town Topic Hamburgers
cards.subtitle: 20th & Broadway, Crossroads Arts District, Kansas City, MO
cards.notes: Use the restaurant’s location note for an around-the-clock downtown meal stop; it identifies this as its 24/7 location.
cards.short_summary: A historic downtown diner whose official site identifies a 24/7 location.
cards.evidence_claim: Town Topic states that its location at 20th and Broadway in the Crossroads Arts District is open 24 hours, seven days a week.
cards.access_notes: The restaurant’s site describes the 20th & Broadway location as open 24 hours, seven days a week.

cards.title: Big Back Eatery
cards.subtitle: 7208 Prospect Avenue, Kansas City, MO
cards.notes: Plan around the posted late-week carryout schedule; the site lists service through 5 a.m. on Wednesday through Saturday.
cards.short_summary: A Prospect Avenue eatery publishing overnight carryout hours.
cards.evidence_claim: Big Back Eatery lists carryout hours through 5 a.m. Wednesday through Saturday at 7208 Prospect Avenue.
cards.access_notes: Posted carryout hours run midnight–5 a.m. Wednesday and 5 p.m.–5 a.m. Thursday–Saturday.

cards.title: Taco Bell — Prospect Avenue
cards.subtitle: 1420 Prospect Avenue, Kansas City, MO
cards.notes: Use the official restaurant page for a drive-through pickup; it currently lists the drive-through as open 24 hours every day.
cards.short_summary: A 24-hour drive-through option on Prospect Avenue.
cards.evidence_claim: Taco Bell’s official page lists 24-hour drive-through service every day at 1420 Prospect Avenue.
cards.access_notes: Official location page lists drive-through hours as open 24 hours daily; dine-in hours differ.

cards.title: McDonald's — NW 83rd Terrace
cards.subtitle: 6830 NW 83rd Terrace, Kansas City, MO
cards.notes: For an overnight drive-through order, rely on the location’s official schedule rather than lobby hours, which end at 11 p.m.
cards.short_summary: A McDonald’s location with a separately posted 24-hour drive-through.
cards.evidence_claim: McDonald’s lists its drive-through at 6830 NW 83rd Terrace as open 24 hours every day.
cards.access_notes: Drive-through is posted 24 hours daily; restaurant and lobby hours are posted as 5 a.m.–11 p.m.

cards.title: Denny's — Taney Street
cards.subtitle: 2117 Taney Street, Kansas City, MO
cards.notes: Use Denny’s location page when you need an all-hours sit-down or takeout option; it specifically lists round-the-clock breakfast.
cards.short_summary: A 24-hour diner with dine-in and takeout services listed.
cards.evidence_claim: Denny’s lists its restaurant at 2117 Taney Street as open 24 hours and identifies round-the-clock breakfast service.
cards.access_notes: Official location page states “Open 24 Hours” and shows every day as open 24 hours.

cards.title: IHOP — N Chouteau Trafficway
cards.subtitle: 4337 N Chouteau Trafficway, Kansas City, MO
cards.notes: Check the official location page for a 24-hour restaurant option; it lists dine-in, takeout, and late-night food amenities.
cards.short_summary: An IHOP with all-day published hours and late-night food listed.
cards.evidence_claim: IHOP lists its 4337 N Chouteau Trafficway restaurant as open 24 hours every day and offering late-night food.
cards.access_notes: Official page posts “Open 24 Hours” for Monday through Sunday and lists late-night food among amenities.

cards.title: La Bamba Restaurant and Cantina
cards.subtitle: 8500 E. US Highway 40, Kansas City, MO
cards.notes: Use the restaurant’s own business-hours listing for an overnight weekday pickup; it currently posts 24-hour Tuesday and Wednesday availability.
cards.short_summary: An east Kansas City restaurant with published overnight midweek hours.
cards.evidence_claim: La Bamba Restaurant and Cantina lists Tuesday and Wednesday as open 24 hours at 8500 E. US Highway 40.
cards.access_notes: The business’s posted hours list Tuesday and Wednesday as open 24 hours; verify the day-specific schedule before travel.

boards.title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
boards.description: Ten named UMKC places for studying, meeting, recreation, and campus connection, supported by current university and library sources.

cards.entity_name: Miller Nichols Library Second Floor Silent Study Area
cards.title: Miller Nichols Library silent-study floor
cards.subtitle: Miller Nichols Library, 800 E. 51st St.
cards.notes: Bring independent work and headphones: this designated silent area does not allow conversation, group study, or cell-phone talking.
cards.short_summary: A named silent-study floor for focused individual work.
cards.evidence_claim: UMKC Libraries designates the second floor of Miller Nichols Library as a silent area.
cards.access_notes: Available while the library is open; follow the posted silent-study expectations.

cards.title: Digital Collaboration Studio
cards.subtitle: Third floor, Miller Nichols Library
cards.notes: Use the mobile furniture, HD monitors, digital whiteboard, or reservable rooms when a project needs shared screens or remote collaboration.
cards.short_summary: A technology-equipped library space for study, meetings, and collaborative work.
cards.evidence_claim: The third-floor studio has an open area, HD monitors, a video-conferencing seminar room, and small collaboration rooms.
cards.source_title: Now Open! Digital Collaboration Studio - UMKC Libraries
cards.access_notes: Open for work, study, meetings, or collaboration when Miller Nichols Library is open; some rooms are reservable.

cards.title: Victor Wilson Learning Collaborative
cards.subtitle: Fourth floor, Miller Nichols Library
cards.notes: Meet a study group in the open areas or reserve a technology-enabled room; academic-support and mentoring programs are located on this floor.
cards.short_summary: A renovated fourth-floor hub combining study seating, meeting rooms, and student-support programs.
cards.evidence_claim: The collaborative includes open study areas, meeting rooms, laptop stations, and dedicated student-support program spaces.
cards.source_title: UMKC Unveils Victor Wilson Learning Collaborative to Boost Student Achievement
cards.access_notes: Study and meeting spaces are open during library hours; reserve rooms in advance where required.

cards.title: Music/Media Library
cards.subtitle: Ground floor, Miller Nichols Library
cards.notes: Set up near the listening/viewing resources, or use the computer lab’s music notation software when coursework calls for score or media work.
cards.short_summary: A ground-floor library destination with music and media resources plus specialized software.
cards.evidence_claim: The Music/Media Library includes a computer lab with music notation software, printing, scanners, and headphones for checkout.
cards.access_notes: Located on the library ground floor; consult library hours before visiting.

cards.title: UMKC Student Union
cards.subtitle: 5100 Cherry St., Volker Campus
cards.notes: Use the Union as a practical between-class meeting point for studying, meeting friends, campus resources, food, or scheduled events.
cards.short_summary: The central campus building combines lounges, meeting spaces, services, dining, and event venues.
cards.evidence_claim: UMKC describes the Student Union as a place to study, meet friends, eat, and use campus resources.
cards.access_notes: Public building access and room availability vary by operating hours and scheduled events.

cards.title: Student Union rooftop terrace
cards.subtitle: UMKC Student Union, 5100 Cherry St.
cards.notes: Check the Union’s open areas for a change of scene between classes, and use the terrace only when it is open and not reserved for an event.
cards.short_summary: A named outdoor Union amenity in the campus community hub.
cards.evidence_claim: UMKC’s student handbook lists a roof-top terrace among the Student Union’s spaces.
cards.access_notes: Access depends on Student Union operating conditions and scheduled use; respect posted restrictions.

cards.title: Student Union Gaming Area
cards.subtitle: Level 2, UMKC Student Union
cards.notes: Bring your UMKC ID to the Welcome Desk to check out pool or table-tennis equipment, then return everything after playing.
cards.short_summary: A Level 2 recreation area with billiards and table tennis.
cards.evidence_claim: The Student Union places billiards and table-tennis tables next to Starbucks on Level 2 and offers billiards free to students during operating hours.
cards.access_notes: Students need a UMKC ID to check out equipment at the Welcome Desk; use is during Union operating hours.

cards.title: MindBody Connection
cards.subtitle: Student Union Rooms 303G and 303H
cards.notes: Drop in for a quiet reset with art supplies or massage chairs, and use the space to learn campus-supported stress-management skills.
cards.short_summary: A Student Union wellness space for mindfulness and stress-management support.
cards.evidence_claim: UMKC says the MindBody Connection provides massage chairs, art supplies, and a quiet space for students.
cards.access_notes: Listed hours are Monday–Friday, 8 a.m.–7 p.m.; hours may vary.

cards.title: The Quad
cards.subtitle: Volker Campus green space bounded by Scofield, Newcomb, Royall, Haag, and Flarsheim halls
cards.notes: Use the blue and gold chairs for a short outdoor conversation or pause between classes, keeping pathways clear for others moving through campus.
cards.short_summary: A named Volker Campus quadrangle surrounded by core academic buildings.
cards.evidence_claim: UMKC defines the Quad as the Volker Campus area bounded by Scofield, Newcomb, Royall, Haag, and Flarsheim halls.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor space; availability can be affected by weather and university events.

cards.title: Swinney Recreation Center
cards.subtitle: 5030 Holmes St., Volker Campus
cards.notes: Use the recreation center for fitness, courts, track, or aquatic activities; bring your student ID and check Campus Recreation details before heading over.
cards.short_summary: UMKC’s campus recreation facility with fitness, court, track, and aquatic amenities.
cards.evidence_claim: UMKC states that Campus Recreation at Swinney includes athletic courts, fitness equipment, an indoor track, and an aquatic center.
cards.source_title: Student Success Services - UMKC Academic Catalog
cards.access_notes: Student access and activity availability are managed by UMKC Campus Recreation; check current facility information before visiting.

boards.title: Zero Dollars: 10 Hangs That Cost Nothing
boards.description: No-admission UMKC activities and nearby public art stops, with student-access requirements noted.

cards.title: Play billiards at the Student Union
cards.subtitle: Level 2, UMKC Student Union
cards.notes: Bring a UMKC ID to the Welcome Desk, check out the pool equipment, and return it when your game wraps up.
cards.short_summary: A campus pool-table session with equipment checkout included.
cards.evidence_claim: UMKC states that students can enjoy billiards free of charge during Student Union operating hours with ID-based equipment checkout.
cards.access_notes: UMKC student ID is required to check out equipment at the Welcome Desk; available during operating hours.

cards.title: Set up a table-tennis game
cards.subtitle: Level 2, UMKC Student Union
cards.notes: Meet beside Starbucks on Level 2, then use your UMKC ID at the Welcome Desk to borrow table-tennis accessories.
cards.short_summary: A bring-a-friend ping-pong stop in the Union.
cards.evidence_claim: UMKC lists table tennis next to Starbucks on Student Union Level 2 and says students may check out accessories with their UMKC ID.
cards.access_notes: Present a UMKC ID at the Welcome Desk and return borrowed accessories after use.

cards.title: Join an intramural team or tournament
cards.subtitle: Campus Recreation, Swinney Center
cards.notes: Check the RooSports options, gather a team or sign up solo where available, and use the activity for low-stakes competition.
cards.short_summary: UMKC’s student intramural-sports program.
cards.evidence_claim: Campus Recreation says all UMKC fee-paying students can participate in intramurals for free.
cards.access_notes: Free for UMKC fee-paying students; non-students need a Campus Recreation membership and sports pass.

cards.title: Take a group fitness class together
cards.subtitle: Swinney Center
cards.notes: Choose a Campus Recreation class that fits your schedule and arrive ready to participate with a classmate or roommate.
cards.short_summary: Student group fitness at no extra charge.
cards.evidence_claim: UMKC reports that students can participate in group fitness classes at no extra cost.
cards.source_title: Campus Resources for Student Success and Wellness
cards.access_notes: For UMKC students; Campus Recreation facilities are in the Swinney Center.

cards.title: Cheer at a Kansas City home game
cards.subtitle: UMKC athletics venues
cards.notes: Check the home schedule, bring your student ID, and make a group plan around a Kansas City Athletics game.
cards.short_summary: Student-ID entry to UMKC’s Division I home games.
cards.evidence_claim: UMKC states that students enjoy free admission to all Kansas City Athletics home games with their student ID.
cards.access_notes: Free for UMKC students with student ID; confirm the sport’s home schedule and venue before going.

cards.title: Ride the campus shuttle between stops
cards.subtitle: Volker and Hospital Hill campuses
cards.notes: Use the shuttle to link a study stop, campus errand, or lunch plan without arranging a separate ride between campuses.
cards.short_summary: Free student transportation connecting UMKC campuses.
cards.evidence_claim: UMKC says its shuttle provides free transportation for students around the Volker and Hospital Hill campuses.
cards.source_title: Campus Resources for Student Success and Wellness
cards.access_notes: For students; UMKC says the route includes residential halls and prominent campus locations.

cards.title: Go to a Roos After Dark takeover
cards.subtitle: UMKC Student Union
cards.notes: Watch the event calendar for a Union takeover, then go with friends for the scheduled activities and entertainment.
cards.short_summary: A late-evening Student Union program with activities.
cards.evidence_claim: UMKC describes Roos After Dark Union Takeovers as Student Union events with free food, entertainment, and interactive activities.
cards.access_notes: Event availability varies; consult UMKC’s events calendar for a scheduled takeover.

cards.title: Catch a Union Programming Board event
cards.subtitle: UMKC campus and Kansas City outings
cards.notes: Follow UPB through RooGroups, choose a listed program, and use it as an easy way to meet up around an activity.
cards.short_summary: Student-run entertainment and social programs.
cards.evidence_claim: UMKC RooGroups says the Union Programming Board hosts fun and free events on and off campus.
cards.access_notes: Open event details, timing, and participation requirements vary by program; check RooGroups before attending.

cards.title: Start with Jump Into UMKC
cards.subtitle: UMKC Volker Campus
cards.notes: Incoming undergraduates can register after orientation, then use the multi-day program to meet peers through scheduled group activities.
cards.short_summary: A no-cost onboarding program for new UMKC undergraduates.
cards.evidence_claim: UMKC’s 2026 Jump Into UMKC listing says there is no cost to attend for incoming new-to-UMKC undergraduates who completed orientation and enrolled in fall courses.
cards.access_notes: Limited to eligible incoming, new-to-UMKC undergraduates who completed orientation and enrolled in fall courses; registration is required.

cards.title: Browse the Nelson-Atkins collection
cards.subtitle: 4525 Oak St., Kansas City
cards.notes: Meet in the galleries or pair the collection with a walk on the museum grounds; skip ticketed special exhibitions unless you choose to pay.
cards.short_summary: A nearby art-museum visit with free general admission.
cards.evidence_claim: The Nelson-Atkins says member support keeps general admission to the museum free for everyone.
cards.source_title: Teens, Volunteers, Membership - Nelson-Atkins Museum of Art
cards.access_notes: General admission is free; some special exhibitions, programs, and parking may have separate charges.

boards.title: Claimed by 9am: 10 Study Spots Worth Showing Up Early For
boards.description: Ten documented UMKC library environments for solo work, group sessions, and technology-supported research.

cards.entity_name: Miller Nichols Library Ground Floor Study Spaces
cards.title: Ground Floor Study Spaces
cards.subtitle: Miller Nichols Library · quiet conversation
cards.notes: Set up near the Marr Sound Archives when you need an individual table, chair, nearby vending, and wall outlets for a longer work block.
cards.short_summary: Individual tables with outlets on the library’s quiet-conversation floor.
cards.evidence_claim: UMKC Libraries lists multiple individual study spaces with tables, chairs, vending machines, and wall outlets on Miller Nichols Library’s Ground Floor; open spaces are not reservable.
cards.access_notes: Open study spaces are not reservable; follow the quiet-conversation volume level.

cards.title: Study Room 108A
cards.subtitle: Miller Nichols Library · First Floor
cards.notes: Reserve this enclosed room for a small project meeting when a monitor, webcam, whiteboard, and device connections will keep everyone working together.
cards.short_summary: An enclosed six-person room with presentation and whiteboard tools.
cards.evidence_claim: Study Room 108A seats 1–6 and includes a large monitor/computer, webcam, table, chairs, whiteboard, and HDMI, USB-C, and wireless connections.
cards.access_notes: Located on the First Floor; library rooms may be reserved for up to two hours per group per day.

cards.entity_name: Miller Nichols Library Second Floor Silent Study
cards.title: Second Floor Silent Study
cards.subtitle: Miller Nichols Library · silent-study floor
cards.notes: Bring headphones and choose a table near the rolling or wall-mounted whiteboards for independent work that needs a fully silent setting.
cards.short_summary: Silent individual study with tables and whiteboards.
cards.evidence_claim: UMKC Libraries designates the Second Floor of Miller Nichols Library for silent study and provides wall-mounted whiteboards, rolling whiteboards, and tables.
cards.access_notes: No conversation, group study, or cell-phone talking is allowed in designated silent-study areas.

cards.title: Active Study Room
cards.subtitle: Miller Nichols Library · Second Floor
cards.notes: Use this named Second Floor destination when you want a study stop distinct from the surrounding silent floor; confirm current room availability before heading over.
cards.short_summary: A named study-room destination on Miller Nichols Library’s silent-study floor.
cards.evidence_claim: UMKC’s Miller Nichols Library floor plan lists an Active Study Room among the Second Floor destinations, whose volume level is designated silent study.
cards.access_notes: Located on the Second Floor; use the library floor plan and Service Desk for current wayfinding or availability help.

cards.title: Digital Collaboration Studio Common Area
cards.subtitle: Miller Nichols Library · Third Floor
cards.notes: Check in at the Studio desk, then use the drop-in common area for collaborative research with mobile furniture, monitors, and a digital whiteboard.
cards.short_summary: A drop-in collaboration area with flexible furniture and digital displays.
cards.evidence_claim: The Digital Collaboration Studio’s common area is available on a drop-in basis and includes mobile furniture, high-definition monitors, and a mobile digital whiteboard.
cards.access_notes: For UMKC faculty, staff, and students; check in on arrival. It is a quiet-conversation area and requires closed drink containers.

cards.title: Collaboration Room 310A
cards.subtitle: Digital Collaboration Studio · Third Floor
cards.notes: Book this small room for a focused group session and connect a laptop to the Vibe Board when a shared screen and video call tools are useful.
cards.short_summary: A reservable four-person collaboration room with a Vibe Board.
cards.evidence_claim: Digital Collaboration Studio Room 310A seats up to four and has a laptop-connectable Vibe Board plus camera-and-speaker teleconferencing technology.
cards.access_notes: UMKC students, staff, and faculty may reserve it for up to two hours per group per day using UMKC credentials.

cards.title: Collaboration Room 310B
cards.subtitle: Digital Collaboration Studio · Third Floor
cards.notes: Reserve this quiet-conversation room for a four-person-or-smaller team, especially when your session needs a shared digital board and teleconferencing setup.
cards.short_summary: A second reservable, technology-equipped small-group room in the Studio.
cards.evidence_claim: Digital Collaboration Studio Room 310B seats up to four and is equipped with a laptop-connectable Vibe Board and camera-and-speaker teleconferencing technology.
cards.access_notes: UMKC students, staff, and faculty may reserve it for up to two hours per group per day using UMKC credentials.

cards.entity_name: Miller Nichols Library Fourth Floor Study Areas
cards.title: Fourth Floor Study Areas
cards.subtitle: Miller Nichols Library · regular conversation
cards.notes: Choose a table, soft seating, or a reservable group room on the renovated floor when you want nearby power and a setting suited to collaborative work.
cards.short_summary: Renovated group-friendly study areas with flexible seating and reservable rooms.
cards.evidence_claim: The renovated Fourth Floor has study areas, 304 student-study seats, technology-enabled rooms, nearby outlets, and reservable group rooms for 3–8 people.
cards.access_notes: Study spaces are open while the library is open; many rooms can be reserved up to one week ahead in two-hour blocks.

cards.entity_name: Health Sciences Library Silent Study Area
cards.title: Health Sciences Library Silent Study
cards.subtitle: Health Sciences Library · north end
cards.notes: Head to the north-end silent area for uninterrupted individual work, and keep calls, conversation, and group work outside the designated zone.
cards.short_summary: A designated silent area in UMKC’s Health Sciences Library.
cards.evidence_claim: UMKC Libraries identifies the north end of the Health Sciences Library as a designated silent area; its floor plan also lists a Silent Study Area.
cards.access_notes: No conversation, group study, or cell-phone talking is allowed in designated silent-study areas.

cards.entity_name: Health Sciences Library Active Study Room
cards.title: Health Sciences Library Active Study Room
cards.subtitle: Health Sciences Library · south end
cards.notes: Ask at the Service Desk before using this active-work option, which pairs two treadmill desks with a standing desk for a change of study posture.
cards.short_summary: An active-work study room with treadmill and standing desks.
cards.evidence_claim: The Health Sciences Library’s Active Study Room at the south end has two treadmill desks and one standing desk.
cards.access_notes: The library is open 24 hours daily with card access to the School of Medicine building; ask the Service Desk for room information.

boards.title: 10 Blocks Off Campus, One Reason Each
boards.description: Ten named destinations along the Main, Oak, Warwick, Rockhill, Cherry, and 43rd Street corridors bordering UMKC’s Volker campus.

cards.title: The Nelson-Atkins Museum of Art
cards.subtitle: Oak Street corridor, near 45th Street
cards.notes: Walk the Oak Street corridor to enter the museum and use its detailed visitor map to choose galleries, accessibility options, or a timed visit.
cards.short_summary: A nearby art museum with free general admission and a substantial permanent collection.
cards.evidence_claim: The Nelson-Atkins states that visitors can see more than 5,000 years of art for free and provides museum visitor information.
cards.source_title: Plan your visit to The Nelson-Atkins Museum of Art
cards.access_notes: Check the museum’s visit page for current daily hours, gallery closures, and entry guidance.

cards.title: Donald J. Hall Sculpture Park
cards.subtitle: Oak Street corridor, south of the Nelson-Atkins
cards.notes: Use the south lawn paths from Oak Street to see the outdoor monumental works, including the shuttlecock sculptures, during daylight.
cards.short_summary: An outdoor sculpture destination beside the Nelson-Atkins campus-facing route.
cards.evidence_claim: The Nelson-Atkins identifies the Donald J. Hall Sculpture Park as free to visit and open from sunrise to sundown.
cards.source_title: Plan your visit to The Nelson-Atkins Museum of Art
cards.access_notes: Outdoor access is listed as sunrise to sundown; follow museum grounds rules.

cards.title: Kemper Museum of Contemporary Art
cards.subtitle: Warwick Boulevard corridor, near 44th Street
cards.notes: Approach on Warwick Boulevard and check the museum’s current exhibition information before going; the venue’s free-access model covers its exhibitions.
cards.short_summary: A contemporary-art museum at 4420 Warwick Boulevard, just north of UMKC’s orbit.
cards.evidence_claim: Kemper Museum’s official 2026 event information states that museum admission is always free and gives its address as 4420 Warwick Boulevard.
cards.source_title: Kemper Museum Gala: Know Before You Go
cards.access_notes: Confirm current gallery hours and exhibition availability with Kemper before visiting.

cards.entity_name: Emily & Todd Voth Artspace at KCAI
cards.title: Emily & Todd Voth Artspace at KCAI
cards.subtitle: 43rd Street corridor at Walnut Street
cards.notes: Follow 43rd Street to the KCAI exhibition space and check its program calendar for current shows, talks, and any visit-specific guidance.
cards.short_summary: A KCAI contemporary-art venue renamed in 2025 and positioned at 16 East 43rd Street.
cards.evidence_claim: Kansas City Art Institute says the Emily & Todd Voth Artspace at 16 East 43rd Street provides free and accessible arts programming.
cards.source_title: KCAI’s Artspace Announces Bold New Era with Renaming to The Emily & Todd Voth Artspace
cards.access_notes: Review current exhibition and event details before arrival.

cards.title: Community Christian Church
cards.subtitle: Main Street corridor at 46th Street
cards.notes: Pause along Main Street to view the Frank Lloyd Wright-designed sanctuary, then consult the church schedule if you plan to attend worship or arts programming.
cards.short_summary: A National Register-listed Frank Lloyd Wright building at 4601 Main Street.
cards.evidence_claim: Community Christian Church says its sanctuary was designed by Frank Lloyd Wright and identifies its location as 4601 Main Street.
cards.source_title: Community Christian Church: Frank Lloyd Wright
cards.access_notes: The building is an active church; use posted service and program information for interior access.

cards.entity_name: Plaza Branch, Kansas City Public Library
cards.title: Plaza Branch
cards.subtitle: Main Street corridor at 48th Street
cards.notes: Enter from Main Street to browse, study by the floor-to-ceiling windows, and locate the permanent “Good As Gold” book sculpture in the foyer.
cards.short_summary: A public-library branch at 4801 Main Street with a permanent sculpture made of books.
cards.evidence_claim: Kansas City Public Library lists Plaza Branch at 4801 Main Street and identifies “Good As Gold” as a permanent foyer sculpture there.
cards.source_title: Plaza Branch | Kansas City Public Library
cards.access_notes: The library lists current hours on its location page; visitors should observe library policies.

cards.entity_name: Ewing and Muriel Kauffman Memorial Garden
cards.title: Ewing and Muriel Kauffman Memorial Garden
cards.subtitle: Rockhill Road corridor, near 48th Street
cards.notes: Use the Rockhill Road entrance for a garden walk, then follow posted on-site rules while visiting the memorial landscape and adjoining foundation campus.
cards.short_summary: A memorial garden on the Kauffman Foundation campus at 4801 Rockhill Road.
cards.evidence_claim: The Ewing Marion Kauffman Foundation identifies the Memorial Garden as part of its 4801 Rockhill Road campus and describes it as the final resting place of Ewing and Muriel Kauffman.
cards.source_title: Our Campus | Ewing Marion Kauffman Foundation
cards.access_notes: Check the garden’s current visitor information before making a dedicated trip.

cards.title: Linda Hall Library
cards.subtitle: Cherry Street corridor at 51st Street
cards.notes: Bring photo ID if you want borrowing access, or use the Main Reading Room, study rooms, and public browsing areas during listed library hours.
cards.short_summary: A science, engineering, and technology library at 5109 Cherry Street that welcomes public research visits.
cards.evidence_claim: Linda Hall Library states that it is open to the public free of charge and that its Main Reading Room and study rooms are open to visitors.
cards.access_notes: The library lists public hours as Monday–Friday, 10 a.m.–5 p.m.; rare-book use requires an appointment.

cards.title: Linda Hall Library Arboretum
cards.subtitle: Cherry Street corridor at 51st Street
cards.notes: Take a grounds walk around the library to see labeled tree diversity and tree peonies; keep pets leashed and leave picnics and hammocks at home.
cards.short_summary: A 14-acre urban arboretum surrounding Linda Hall Library with more than 300 trees.
cards.evidence_claim: Linda Hall Library says its 14-acre arboretum has more than 300 trees and that the grounds are open to the public from 5 a.m. to 11 p.m.
cards.access_notes: Grounds are listed as open 5 a.m.–11 p.m.; comply with the library’s grounds rules.

cards.entity_name: The National Museum of Toys and Miniatures
cards.title: The National Museum of Toys and Miniatures
cards.subtitle: Oak Street corridor at 52nd Street
cards.notes: Use the 52nd Street entrance for the museum lot, reserve tickets if needed, and allow time for the first-floor miniatures and second-floor toy galleries.
cards.short_summary: A two-floor museum at 5235 Oak Street on the southwest corner of the UMKC campus.
cards.evidence_claim: The National Museum of Toys and Miniatures says it is at 5235 Oak Street, on UMKC’s southwest campus corner, with two floors devoted to miniatures and toys.
cards.source_title: Plan Your Visit | The National Museum of Toys and Miniatures
cards.access_notes: The museum encourages advance ticket reservations because gallery capacity is limited; parking is listed as free.

boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: Ten officially documented UMKC rituals, symbols and recurring campus traditions that connect Roos across generations.

cards.title: Sing the 2018 fight song
cards.subtitle: A revived song with “Kangarooters” roots
cards.notes: Listen for the fight song at a home athletics event, then join the chorus if you know it. Its 2018 version drew lyrical inspiration from archival “Kangarooters.”
cards.short_summary: A modern UMKC fight song built from an older Kansas City University discovery.
cards.evidence_claim: UMKC says its fight song was newly established in 2018 and was inspired by lyrics from an archival Kansas City University song titled “Kangarooters.”
cards.access_notes: UMKC identifies the song as a mainstay at home athletics events.

cards.title: Make the Roo Up sign
cards.subtitle: Kangaroo ears and nose, made by hand
cards.notes: Raise your index and pinky fingers for ears, then bring the other fingers forward for the nose. Use it in photos or while supporting the Roos at an event.
cards.short_summary: UMKC’s 2018 hand gesture turns a hand into a stylized kangaroo face.
cards.evidence_claim: UMKC calls Roo Up a tradition adopted in 2018 and specifies how the fingers form the kangaroo’s ears and nose.
cards.access_notes: The university says Roo Up appears across campus and at sporting events.

cards.title: Join the alma mater
cards.subtitle: A song first sung to the Men’s Glee Club in 1940
cards.notes: Learn the refrain before a home sporting event and sing with the crowd. The words celebrate UMKC’s blue and gold and connect today’s Roos with earlier classes.
cards.short_summary: A 1940 school song still sung at UMKC home sporting events.
cards.evidence_claim: UMKC states that its alma mater was first sung to the Men’s Glee Club in 1940 and is sung at all UMKC home sporting events.
cards.access_notes: UMKC says the alma mater is sung at all home sporting events.

cards.title: Wear the school colors
cards.subtitle: Student council chose the palette in 1934
cards.notes: Choose Roo blue and gold for a campus event or photo. The color pairing is a student-established part of UMKC identity, reaching back to the university’s early years.
cards.short_summary: UMKC’s official colors have been old gold and royal blue since 1934.
cards.evidence_claim: UMKC says the student council named “old gold and royal blue” the official school colors in 1934 and that they remain in use.
cards.access_notes: This is a school-spirit practice suitable for campus and athletics events.

cards.title: Show up Roo Blue on Friday
cards.subtitle: The weekly blue-and-gold spirit cue
cards.notes: Plan a Roo blue item for Friday and wear it around campus or at a Roos event. Keep the look simple: the tradition is the shared color, not a required outfit.
cards.short_summary: A Friday ritual of wearing Roo Blue in support of the KC Roos.
cards.evidence_claim: UMKC defines Roo Blue Fridays as Fridays when the campus wears Roo Blue to support the KC Roos.
cards.access_notes: Observed on Fridays; participation is a personal apparel choice.

cards.title: Spot the KC Roo
cards.subtitle: The 1937 kangaroo mascot with a Disney connection
cards.notes: Look for the mascot at a campus gathering or athletics event, and notice the classic Roo imagery too. The Roo story began before UMKC had an athletics department.
cards.short_summary: UMKC’s kangaroo mascot dates to 1937 and its original version was drawn by Walt Disney.
cards.evidence_claim: UMKC says Kasey the Kangaroo, now known as the KC Roo, became UKC’s official mascot in 1937 and that Walt Disney drafted the original version.
cards.access_notes: The mascot is associated with campus and sporting-event spirit activity.

cards.title: Mark UMKC’s anniversary week
cards.subtitle: Late October campus-and-city celebration
cards.notes: Check the university calendar during the last week in October and choose an event that fits your schedule. Activities have included arts, athletics, service and alumni programs.
cards.short_summary: A long-standing late-October tradition commemorating UMKC’s anniversary.
cards.evidence_claim: UMKC describes Blue and Gold Week as a long-standing tradition during the last week in October that commemorates the university’s anniversary.
cards.access_notes: UMKC says activities take place on both campuses and around Kansas City during the last week in October.

cards.title: Look for the Regalia Run
cards.subtitle: A Blue and Gold Week annual event
cards.notes: Watch Blue and Gold Week announcements for the annual Regalia Run and follow the event’s posted participation details. It is one of the named activities in UMKC’s anniversary-week program.
cards.short_summary: The annual Regalia Run is a named component of UMKC’s Blue and Gold Week.
cards.evidence_claim: UMKC lists the annual Regalia Run among the activities held for Blue and Gold Week.
cards.access_notes: Check current Blue and Gold Week event details before participating.

cards.title: Document your Traditions Challenge
cards.subtitle: A photo-based UMKC experience checklist
cards.notes: Enroll through RooGroups, photograph each completed item, and submit your progress there. The challenge is designed to connect participants with campus and Kansas City experiences.
cards.short_summary: UMKC’s challenge asks students to document distinct traditions and experiences.
cards.evidence_claim: UMKC instructs participants to sign up in RooGroups, take photos while completing list items and submit those photos to track progress.
cards.access_notes: Registration and photo submission are handled through RooGroups; review current challenge requirements there.

cards.title: Earn Traditions Keeper status
cards.subtitle: A graduation-year celebration for challenge completers
cards.notes: If you complete the Traditions Challenge, follow the listed graduation-semester deadline and contact the program as directed. Eligible graduating students are invited to the annual celebration.
cards.short_summary: Graduating students who finish the challenge can be recognized as Traditions Keepers.
cards.evidence_claim: UMKC says graduating students who complete the Traditions Challenge are invited to a celebratory ceremony each year as Traditions Keepers.
cards.access_notes: UMKC lists completion deadlines of March 31 for spring graduation and October 31 for fall graduation.

boards.title: Your First Weekend at University of Missouri-Kansas City, Shared as Cards
boards.description: A low-pressure first-weekend sequence that starts on the Volker Campus and opens into nearby Kansas City art, gardens, and public spaces.

cards.title: Start with a game at the Student Union
cards.subtitle: Friday afternoon · UMKC Student Union, Level 2
cards.notes: Bring your UMKC ID to the Welcome Desk, check out pool or table-tennis equipment, and use a game to make an easy first introduction.
cards.short_summary: A campus-based icebreaker with equipment checkout handled at the Welcome Desk.
cards.evidence_claim: UMKC says billiards tables and table tennis are on Level 2 by Starbucks, and students may use billiards free during operating hours with a UMKC ID.
cards.access_notes: Show a UMKC ID at the Welcome Desk to check out equipment; use is during Student Union operating hours.

cards.title: Make dinner plans at Foodiverse
cards.subtitle: Friday early evening · UMKC Student Union
cards.notes: Walk the Foodiverse counters together and choose a meal that fits your appetite; use this stop to keep the first evening on campus.
cards.short_summary: A multi-counter dining stop inside the Student Union.
cards.evidence_claim: UMKC lists Student Union Foodiverse dining options including Simple Servings, Cherry St. Deli, Joey's Pizza & Pasta, Fresh Harvest, Union Grill Co. and 7 Spoons.
cards.access_notes: Food service is located in the UMKC Student Union; check the dining service for current operating details.

cards.title: Settle in at Miller Nichols Library
cards.subtitle: Friday evening · 800 E. 51st St.
cards.notes: Choose an individual or group study area, connect to the library Wi-Fi, and make a short plan for the first week before heading out.
cards.short_summary: UMKC's largest library offers study seating and campus collections.
cards.evidence_claim: Miller Nichols Library is UMKC's largest library and provides Wi-Fi plus seating for individual and group study.
cards.access_notes: The library lists daily hours separately; consult its current hours before visiting.

cards.title: See what is on view at UMKC Gallery of Art
cards.subtitle: Friday daytime · Fine Arts Building, Room 203
cards.notes: Stop by during gallery hours, take in the current work, and check the exhibition information for an artist or idea worth discussing afterward.
cards.short_summary: A public campus exhibition space for guest and student artists.
cards.evidence_claim: UMKC describes the UMKC Gallery of Art as a public exhibition space featuring guest and student artists, open during regular gallery hours or by appointment.
cards.access_notes: The gallery lists Monday-Friday hours and is closed Saturdays and Sundays except by appointment.

cards.title: Move around at Swinney Center
cards.subtitle: Saturday morning · 5030 Holmes St.
cards.notes: Use the fitness center, track, courts, or pool as your schedule and recreation access allow, then borrow any needed equipment at the service center.
cards.short_summary: Campus recreation facilities provide several indoor ways to reset on a weekend.
cards.evidence_claim: UMKC lists a fitness center, multipurpose courts, indoor track, 25-yard lap pool, studios, sauna and equipment checkout at Swinney Center.
cards.access_notes: Listed weekend hours are Saturday 9 a.m.-6 p.m. and Sunday noon-6 p.m.; recreation membership or an applicable day pass is required.

cards.entity_name: Ewing and Muriel Kauffman Memorial Garden
cards.title: Walk the Kauffman Memorial Garden
cards.subtitle: Saturday midday · 4801 Rockhill Road
cards.notes: Follow the brick walkways at an unhurried pace, notice the changing plantings and bronze sculptures, and respect the garden's no-alcohol policy.
cards.short_summary: A public garden with seasonal displays, fountains, and sculpture near campus.
cards.evidence_claim: The Kauffman Memorial Garden welcomes all ages and states that admission and parking are free; it features seasonal plantings, fountains and bronze sculptures.
cards.source_title: Ewing and Muriel Kauffman Memorial Garden
cards.access_notes: All ages are welcome. The garden prohibits alcoholic drinks, biking, and rollerblading.

cards.title: Explore the Nelson-Atkins galleries
cards.subtitle: Saturday afternoon · 4525 Oak St.
cards.notes: Check in at an entrance, pick a gallery wing or collection to explore, and leave time to walk outside among the sculpture park installations.
cards.short_summary: A nearby art museum where general-admission galleries are available without an admission charge.
cards.evidence_claim: The Nelson-Atkins states that admission is free every day for everyone, with check-in required for access to general-admission galleries.
cards.source_title: Plan Your Visit to The Nelson-Atkins Museum of Art
cards.access_notes: Check in online or at the museum before entering galleries; museum hours vary by day.

cards.entity_name: Laura Conyers Smith Municipal Rose Garden
cards.title: Take a Loose Park garden loop
cards.subtitle: Saturday late afternoon · Loose Park
cards.notes: Walk to the municipal rose garden, take in the planted beds and fountains, and keep food and picnics outside the rose-garden area.
cards.short_summary: A named garden within Loose Park with thousands of roses and historic roots.
cards.evidence_claim: Kansas City Parks identifies the Laura Conyers Smith Municipal Rose Garden as a Loose Park amenity and says it contains about 3,000 roses in nearly 130 varieties.
cards.access_notes: Loose Park lists hours of 5 a.m.-midnight daily; no food or picnics are allowed in the Rose Garden.

cards.title: Ride the KC Streetcar to see the corridor
cards.subtitle: Saturday evening · UMKC to River Market route
cards.notes: Board at a marked stop, use the ride to orient yourself along Main Street, and check the live service information before planning a return trip.
cards.short_summary: A fare-free streetcar route connecting UMKC with destinations north along Main Street.
cards.evidence_claim: KC Streetcar states that there is no fare to ride from UMKC to the River Market and lists Friday and Saturday service until 1 a.m.
cards.access_notes: Listed Friday and Saturday service runs 5 a.m.-1 a.m.; verify service alerts before travel.

cards.entity_name: Kansas City Public Library Plaza Branch
cards.title: Wrap up at Plaza Branch
cards.subtitle: Sunday afternoon · 4801 Main St.
cards.notes: Find a window seat or study pod, browse the arts resources, and pause by the Good As Gold book sculpture before heading back toward campus.
cards.short_summary: A public library branch near the Plaza with study resources, events, and a book-based sculpture.
cards.evidence_claim: The Plaza Branch lists youth and arts resources, study pods, Wi-Fi, the Good As Gold book sculpture, and Sunday hours of 11 a.m.-6 p.m.
cards.source_title: Plaza Branch | Kansas City Public Library
cards.access_notes: Listed Sunday hours are 11 a.m.-6 p.m. The branch also lists free parking in its parking garage.
